findings.evidence: `roadmap/TauCetiRoadmap/OneParameterSemigroups/README.md:189-192` specifies `-- theorem bernstein ... ∃! μ`; `code/TauCeti/Analysis/CompletelyMonotone/BernsteinTheorem.lean:680-682` defines `theorem bernstein ... ↔ ∃ μ`, while `:686-688` puts the unique version under `bernstein_unique`.
findings.fix: Change `bernstein` to the unique statement `IsClosedCompletelyMonotone f ↔ ∃! μ : Measure ℝ≥0, RepresentsLaplace f μ`; keep the non-unique theorem under `hausdorff_bernstein_widder` or another explicitly non-unique alias, and make `bernstein_unique` an alias or remove the duplicate name.
findings.issue: `bernstein` is documented as the roadmap-facing name but states only `∃ μ`, so users importing the advertised theorem do not get the uniqueness API the roadmap requires.

summary: The public roadmap-facing name is still assigned to the weaker existence theorem, while the roadmap reserves `bernstein` for the unique finite representing measure statement.
